assurance_statement: This register maps current public first-party evidence to selected framework themes for reviewer orientation. It is not a certification, attestation, audit opinion, penetration test, or claim of full framework conformance.

status_vocabulary.implemented_first_party: Implemented in the public repository and supported by named first-party tests or machine evidence.
status_vocabulary.documented_control: A documented policy or control boundary exists; operating effectiveness is not independently established.
status_vocabulary.partial_or_scoped: Selected controls or a bounded scope are implemented; the framework or product-wide requirement is not fully assessed.
status_vocabulary.prepared_not_executed: A protocol or handoff exists, but the independent, live, or buyer-owned execution has not occurred.
status_vocabulary.buyer_specific_gate: The control must be completed for the buyer, data, jurisdiction, and deployment context.
status_vocabulary.open_gap: Required external, legal, commercial, security, or operational evidence is absent.

frameworks.title: NIST Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework
frameworks.reference_use: Voluntary risk-management orientation across GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE. NIST states that AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim NIST approval, complete AI RMF implementation, or an assessed organizational profile.

frameworks.title: NIST AI RMF Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
frameworks.reference_use: Companion GenAI risk orientation for governance, content provenance, measurement, incident disclosure, and third-party risk.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim complete coverage of the profile's risks or recommended actions, model evaluation, or deployment authorization.

frameworks.title: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
frameworks.reference_use: Voluntary cybersecurity risk orientation across GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim a complete CSF Current or Target Profile, maturity rating, external assessment, or risk acceptance.

frameworks.title: NIST Secure Software Development Framework
frameworks.reference_use: Secure-development orientation across Prepare the Organization, Protect the Software, Produce Well-Secured Software, and Respond to Vulnerabilities.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim full SSDF implementation. NIST SP 800-218 Revision 1, which would define SSDF 1.2, remains draft as of this register date.

frameworks.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
frameworks.reference_use: Application-security verification orientation for architecture, access control, validation, configuration, data protection, and logging.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim an ASVS level, requirement-by-requirement assessment, penetration test, or OWASP certification or endorsement.

frameworks.title: OWASP Large Language Model Security Verification Standard
frameworks.reference_use: LLM-system security orientation for configuration, lifecycle, integration, agents and tools, dependencies, and monitoring.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim an LLMSVS level, complete control assessment, complete AI threat model, or OWASP certification or endorsement.

frameworks.title: Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts
frameworks.reference_use: Software supply-chain orientation for source controls, build provenance, artifact identity, and provenance verification.
frameworks.not_claimed: Does not claim any SLSA Source or Build level, complete product provenance, hosted-builder assurance beyond the signed GitHub workflow identity, or a hardened-build guarantee.

controls.topic: Governance, roles, claims, and decision authority
controls.evidence_establishes: The public evidence protocol assigns bounded artifact roles, distinguishes evidence states, rejects authority escalation, and preserves human release and decision gates.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: An enterprise governance program, board oversight, independent control assessment, legal authority, or production authorization.
controls.next_gate: Name buyer-side risk, data, technical, security, and decision owners in an executed sprint scope.

controls.topic: Measurement, evaluation, reproducibility, and failure retention
controls.evidence_establishes: Named public experiments have bounded source identity, pinned reviewer dependencies, replay requirements, failure retention, and first-party receipts.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: Independent scientific validation, correctness of every input, generalization, field performance, or buyer fitness.
controls.next_gate: Obtain one protocol-matched non-author execution and one buyer-owned baseline run with pre-accepted metrics.

controls.topic: Source authorization, data rights, and intended use
controls.evidence_establishes: Templates require written source authorization, intended use, data classification, handling, acceptance, and decision authority before buyer work.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: An executed license, data-processing agreement, legal sufficiency, regulated-data authorization, or consent for any particular dataset.
controls.next_gate: Execute buyer-specific rights, purpose, handling, retention, deletion, and legal terms before data intake.

controls.topic: Secure development and repository change controls
controls.evidence_establishes: Selected repository workflows use pinned actions, read-only permissions, credential-free checkout, automated tests, and diff checks; contribution and security boundaries are documented.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: Full SSDF practice coverage, protected-branch configuration, required independent review for every change, whole-history security, or audited operating effectiveness.
controls.next_gate: Complete a practice-level SSDF assessment and retain repository-setting, review, vulnerability-management, and remediation evidence.

controls.topic: Dependency inventory and scoped software bill of materials
controls.evidence_establishes: The named reviewer computation has hash-locked Python dependencies and a scoped CycloneDX inventory; the current exact 43-file public release has a deterministic CycloneDX 1.6 inventory with one component per allowlisted file. The one retained, successfully verified main-branch signed-SBOM set covers the historical 30-file release at commit 5fff567c11bee65b5b1de5415d8b8935cd2dfab0, not the current release.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: A complete product, VPS operating-system, gateway, container, private-stack, or organization-wide SBOM, continuous vulnerability monitoring, dependency approval, vulnerability status, or production deployment.
controls.next_gate: Inventory deployment runtime layers, add vulnerability triage and exception handling, and periodically re-verify the retained bundles and trusted roots.

controls.evidence_establishes: The public-site release protocol binds files to Git object identity and SHA-256 digests; one retained main-branch GitHub-hosted run binds the exact release archive to Sigstore-signed build provenance and an SBOM attestation, with repository, workflow, ref, source digest, OIDC issuer, and runner constraints verified.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: SLSA Build L1 or higher, signed provenance for any other commit, whole-product or deployment-runtime provenance, hardened or isolated builds, vulnerability status, or a currently matching live deployment.
controls.next_gate: Assess the hosted build against an explicit SLSA level, extend provenance to deployment runtime layers, periodically re-verify trusted roots, and deploy only through the exact human release gate.

controls.topic: Identity, access control, secrets, and runtime activation
controls.evidence_establishes: Source and negative tests define a default-deny operator boundary; consequential runtime repair remains separately phrase- and secret-gated.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: Production secret installation, enterprise federation, least privilege across every component, independent access-control testing, or a repaired live gateway.
controls.next_gate: Verify secret ownership and rotation, deploy buyer-approved identity controls, and retain current live negative-access evidence.

controls.evidence_establishes: The repository publishes a private vulnerability-reporting route, supported-version boundary, and best-effort handling process.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: A response or remediation SLA, bug bounty, continuous scanning program, penetration test, or historical remediation performance.
controls.next_gate: Agree severity, notification, remediation, disclosure, and evidence-retention terms for the buyer engagement.

controls.evidence_establishes: A first-party severity model, containment and recovery boundaries, deterministic CI tabletop, and machine-verifiable incident policy exist.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: A completed live recovery exercise, customer notification performance, business-continuity certification, recovery objective achievement, or external audit.
controls.next_gate: Run a separately authorized live restoration exercise and negotiate buyer-specific response, notification, backup, and recovery objectives.

controls.evidence_establishes: Selected public interfaces have strict parsing, path and schema defenses, default-deny access behavior, and adversarial unit tests.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: An ASVS level, requirement-by-requirement verification, dynamic application test, penetration test, infrastructure assessment, or absence of vulnerabilities.
controls.next_gate: Define the exact buyer-facing application scope and commission requirement-level ASVS verification and independent penetration testing.

controls.evidence_establishes: The documented research and buyer boundaries separate deterministic evidence from custom-model runs, limit tool and action authority, prohibit unapproved confidential-data submission to external AI, and retain human gates.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: An LLMSVS level, full GenAI threat model, prompt-injection resistance, provider assurance, model safety, continuous AI monitoring, or production agent authorization.
controls.next_gate: Inventory each production model, tool, provider, data flow, memory path, and authority; then execute a scoped LLMSVS and adversarial AI-security assessment.

controls.evidence_establishes: Public artifacts exclude private records by policy, and sprint templates require buyer-specific classification, access, transfer, retention, deletion, incident, and provider decisions.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: HIPAA, GDPR, CCPA, CUI, export-control, classified-data, records-management, or other regulated-data compliance or authorization.
controls.next_gate: Complete legal and security review for the actual data, people, sector, geography, and deployment before intake.

controls.evidence_establishes: A bounded non-author execution handoff, receipt contract, and external replication docket are prepared.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: Evaluator assignment or independence, completed non-author execution, external validation, field validation, certification, or buyer acceptance.
controls.next_gate: A qualified non-author evaluator must execute the locked protocol and return a complete verifiable receipt.

controls.topic: External assurance, legal, insurance, and production acceptance
controls.evidence_establishes: The public materials explicitly separate first-party technical evidence from legal, certification, insurance, customer, and production conclusions.
controls.evidence_does_not_establish: SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP, OWASP certification, NIST conformance, penetration testing, legal approval, adequate insurance, signed customer acceptance, cleared payment, or production approval.
controls.next_gate: Obtain buyer-specific legal, IP, insurance, security, regulatory, independent-testing, and production-acceptance review.
